design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - task 1 (factory_order_milestones_and_delays, env_0060 Ridgeline Window & Door). Revision 2 (policy-audit rework round 2; every figure below is the revision-2 value).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1: {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 6]}. Assignment: remake delay notice 6, on-time guarantee claim 6, remake charge 4, branch storage fee 4.

[Why this is a good test] The customer asks for one thing: settle the storage charge for windows that sat at the branch, on the day his installation started. The storage fee (330.00) depends on the on-time guarantee credit the order earned, because its full weeks late lengthen the free storage period ("The storage fee is fixed only after the order carries the on-time guarantee credit it has earned whenever its shipment came in later than the guarantee grace period allows."), and that credit has never been booked. The credit in turn waits on two open obligations hidden in the milestones. The customer specification remake of 2026-06-03 has neither its delay notice ("The guarantee credit is not booked until every remake on the order recorded with cause customer specification error has its delay notice with cause customer specification remake on record.") nor its remake charge ("The guarantee credit is booked only after each remake on the order recorded with cause customer specification error carries its remake charge."). The agent must:
- discover a diamond-shaped tree (notice and charge -> credit -> storage);
- reconcile eleven order milestones, four installation activities and six window rows;
- run business-day calendars over Memorial Day, Juneteenth and 2026-07-03;
- hand the claim to the customer at the right point.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: late-acknowledgment shift, hold-release requote and expedite fee, with their three tools. Claimed here:
- order_ext_remake_delay_notice (record_remake_delay_notice_f2496c0b, agent);
- order_ext_customer_remake_charge (assess_customer_remake_e3e4e81e, agent);
- order_ext_on_time_guarantee_claim (file_on_time_claim_fe24f9ef, user);
- order_ext_branch_storage_fee (assess_branch_storage_97307cec, agent).
The two scopes are disjoint and together cover all seven policies.

[Route-arounds forced by the frozen blueprint]
(a) Customer write: the only customer-owned acts in the charter are pre-production, and task 0 owns the one that carries a number (the expedite). So the on-time guarantee claim is made the homeowner's own act: "A homeowner whose order earns the on-time guarantee credit files the on-time guarantee claim, and that claim books the credit on the order, dated the order's ship date ...". The earning rule is kept: dated the ship date, class guarantee, cap. Audit T1-O5 accepted this as a real industry pattern.
(b) Delay cause: the notice writes the charter's customer_spec_remake. db_schema lists customer_change instead.
(c) Storage exclusion: the base subtracts each day between the moved crew date and the new one, which the computation language cannot sum. The storage policy instead declares, as an overwrite, a 7-day free-period lengthening per company or weather reschedule on the order's installation job (the stop-at-installation clause is kept).

[Rework round 2 - item closure]
- T1-F1 / F-G1 (RED). The weather tier that gave a later customer postponement more relief than weather is deleted, with its rule sentence and binding. The storage policy's method factor is now long_storage_schedule, a published warehouse schedule:
  - more than 4 billable weeks: 4 weeks at the weekly rate per unit, every later week at 1.5 times it;
  - a single week: a one-bay minimum, the weekly rate times the larger of 4 units and the units on the order (revised in round 3);
  - otherwise: linear.
  Customer reschedules give no relief anywhere.
- F-G12. lateness_end_basis and rebuild_start_anchor (date choices) are relabelled parameter. The genuine method factors are now:
  - glass_recutting: the sealed-unit lead runs alongside the frame rebuild (the longer of the two), versus in-house cutting added in sequence;
  - escalation_schedule: banded paid weeks, versus one added week, versus linear;
  - long_storage_schedule: banded, versus one-bay minimum, versus linear;
  - contract_charge_base: unchanged, a value-based charge versus flat plus setup.
- F-G2. The class-relative ladders now give three distinct values in every build class:
  - remake_rate: 0.5x / 1.2x / class rate;
  - capacity_grace: half the class grace / class grace less 2 / class grace;
  - order_size_rate: 85 % / 125 % / class rate.
- F-G3. Reschedule counts are filtered on the order's own install_job_id.
- F-G4 / F-G14:
  - The notice replaced_by now keeps the class remake lead from the remake date for company-cause remakes.
  - The production-start anchor (a "remake" before production) is replaced by a replacement-glass anchor.
  - line_requeue counts company-cause remakes instead of "total - 1".
- T1-O1. A notice never moves the current ship date earlier. The tool keeps the later of the revised date and the standing projection, and the rule says a late-entered notice serves the benchmark only. The terminal current_ship_date stays 2026-08-31 = ship_date.
- T1-O2. The 2026-05-13 factory-defect remake now carries its factory-capacity notice (revised 2026-06-26). The world was re-timed so the chain stays consistent: shipped 2026-08-31, delivered 2026-09-03, installation 2026-11-23, frozen 2026-11-23.
  - Before the remake notice the order carries 3 notices. The rule states that a late-entered notice for an earlier remake records an earlier delay, not a further one, which is the auditor's own F-G11 reading.
- F-G8. A sentence in each affected rule says how the class enumeration or measure is read.
- F-G16. The "escalation weeks added to the full weeks late" wording is gone; full weeks late is the recorded figure.
- T1-O3: unchanged, an observation. The build-stage factor reads the assembly checkpoint as published.

[Problem-tree card]
- Root: order_ext_branch_storage_fee. Its target is assess_branch_storage_97307cec (agent), state_due, assessed on the day installation starts.
- Edge S <- G:
  - value_input, gate credit_weeks, form state.
  - Sentence: "The storage fee is fixed only after the order carries the on-time guarantee credit it has earned ...", affirmative.
  - Exactly one write books an earned credit: the claim (user).
  - False at the opening: shipped 2026-08-31 against committed 2026-05-28, and no credit row.
- Edge G <- D:
  - value_input, gate bm_t.
  - Sentence: "The guarantee credit is not booked until ...", negated.
  - Exactly one write records the customer specification remake cause.
  - False at the opening: no such notice. The notices on record are glass supplier 2026-03-25, factory capacity 2026-05-13 and factory capacity 2026-07-01.
- Edge G <- R:
  - value_input, gate rate.
  - Sentence: "The guarantee credit is booked only after ...", affirmative.
  - Exactly one write books a remake charge.
  - False at the opening: no remake_charge row.
- 3 of the 3 edges are value_input.
- Order: notice (step 9) and charge (step 11) commute; replaying either order gives identical tables. Then the claim (step 13), then storage (step 15).
- Deletion runs:
  - skip the notice: credit 500.00 (cap) instead of 315.00;
  - skip the charge: credit 500.00 instead of 315.00;
  - skip the claim: storage 420.00 instead of 330.00.
- user_scenario raises only storage. The remake, the notice and the guarantee appear only in passive branches.
- The tools validate nothing.

[Base-invariant card]
- Remake notice:
  - Five governing policies, all policy_scope; there are no gates on a delay notice.
  - The overwrite keeps both notice obligations, and keeps the class lead from the remake date for company-cause remakes.
  - The remake is the order's second, within the class maximum of 2.
- Remake charge:
  - customer_charge_basis holds: the cause is customer_spec_error and the acknowledgment was signed 2026-03-06 and 2026-06-05.
  - The expedite and storage gates are retired for remake charges by scoped overwrites.
  - Dated the remake date.
- Claim:
  - guarantee_class holds: Architectural Wood Build carries the guarantee.
  - Overwrites cover the weeks-late sentence and the earning sentence. The remade-units clause and the cap are kept.
- Storage:
  - after_free_period: anchor delivered_date 2026-09-03, 21 days counted from the day after delivery, exclusive. The last free day is 2026-09-24 and the first chargeable day is 2026-09-25, so the gate holds on 2026-11-23.
  - The gate is also named by sibling overwrites, so the solvability script treats it as retired; it is still declared with its evidence.
  - "Never offered inside the free period": not the case here, because the first crew date 2026-09-21 was offered inside the free period.

[Business-object card]
- Customer: Marcus Jaworski.
- Window contract: RW-26-213907 (6600 Wood-Clad, in-home sale, 4 openings, 5,888.00, no discount program).
- Factory order: FO-2026-23518 (Architectural Wood Build, 4 units, delivered).
- Remakes on the order:
  - 2026-05-13 factory_defect, 1 unit: company cause, never charged; counted for the line requeue and for the opening rate tier.
  - 2026-06-03 customer_spec_error, 2 units: the charged object.
- Installation job IJ-2026-24106 (Full-Frame, 4 units, permitted, 1 crew day, started 2026-11-23). It carries a permit fee (not read) and reschedules: company 2026-09-16, weather 2026-10-02, customer 2026-10-08 (the customer released the 2026-10-13 date without a new one, the job returned to opened, and 2026-11-23 was booked afresh later).

[Factor cards]

Claim: result 315.00.

Multi-source factor: permit_wait_allowance. Cross-difficulty factors: window and install.

Near misses:
- the original acknowledgment of 03-06, which predates the remake;
- the 08-20 assembly checkpoint, which postdates the remake;
- the glass-supplier revised date, which does not move the benchmark;
- the customer reschedule, which lengthens nothing.

[Seed rows and why]
- The factory order feeds all four computations.
- The acknowledgments feed the charge basis and the rebuild anchor.
- The glass-supplier notice feeds the glass share.
- The glass-received checkpoint (2026-04-08, all 4 units, i.e. a full-order checkpoint) feeds the build stage.
- The QC failure, the factory-defect remake and its capacity notice (2026-05-13 -> 2026-06-26) feed the requeue, the rate tier and the grace.
- The customer remake is the charged object.
- The capacity notice of 2026-07-01 (-> 2026-08-31, the actual ship) feeds the grace and the late-notice weeks.
- Assembly 08-20 and QC passed 08-27 complete the build history.
- Every projected-date change carries a notice; the customer remake's notice is the one still owed.
- No closure, warranty registration or credit application is due.

[Persona] Marcus Jaworski, a teacher calling at lunch. He volunteers only the storage request. He gives his identity on request: phone 5135550134, then ZIP 45220, or date of birth February 11, 1979 if asked instead. In passive branches he:
- accepts the remake charge and the notice;
- files the claim with exactly the figures the agent gives;
- ends the call when the storage fee is confirmed.

[Standard solution]
1. Locate the customer by phone.
2. Verify with phone and ZIP.
3. Read the factory orders, order milestones, install jobs, install activities, window contracts and window transactions.
4. Record the notice: -97.
5. Charge remake record 2026-06-03: 580.94.
6. Hand over the claim; the customer files 315.00 with 1 week.
7. Book storage: 330.00 for 5 weeks.

[Verification run] The scratch evaluator printed:
- notice => -97, baseline -129;
- charge => 580.94, baseline 972.0;
- claim => 315.0, baseline 0.0, weeks_late 1;
- storage => 330.0, baseline 336.0, billable_weeks 5;
- skipD->G 500.0, skipR->G 500.0, skipG->S 420.0.

Full gate block: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[Rule <-> compute sweep]
- Notice:
  - start_t <- the rebuild-start ladder;
  - frame_lead <- the glass-and-frame sentence;
  - requeue <- the company-cause remake sentence;
  - lead and rev_t <- the lead-sum and counting sentences;
  - result <- the calendar-day figure sentence;
  - the current-ship-date sentence <- the tool body (later of the two dates).
- Claim:
  - grace <- the class-relative grace sentence;
  - rate <- the class-relative rate sentence;
  - paid_weeks <- the escalation schedule;
  - credit <- the order-of-operations sentence (share, then cap, then one rounding).
- Storage:
  - span <- the storage-count sentence;
  - restarts <- the lengthening sentence (this job only);
  - permit_off and rate <- their ladders;
  - storage_charge <- the schedule sentence;
  - result <- the formula sentence (cap, cent).

[Places most easily got wrong]
- Pricing storage before the credit exists.
- Filing the claim before the notice or the charge.
- Charging the factory-defect remake.
- Taking the class grace or the full rate instead of the relative tiers.
- Counting the customer reschedule.
- Billing all 5 weeks at one rate.
- Counting the installation start day.
- Dropping a holiday from the remake lead.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Reading the published rules and the finder returns alone gives the same four figures. The only free choice, the order of notice and charge, gives identical tables.

[Revision log]
- R1: compute syntax fix and verification by ZIP (round 1).
- R2: the round-2 closures listed above.


[Rework round 3 - item closure]
- F-1 (render source) / R2-G3: the remake charge's build-stage rule is now exhaustive and identical to the compute. It reads only checkpoints covering every unit on the order, so replacement glass for remade units does not count. The tiers: the most recent such assembly checkpoint on or before the remake date gives the full charge; otherwise the most recent such glass checkpoint on or before it gives 70 percent; otherwise 40 percent. The compute filters LATEST on unit_count = the order's units. On this world glass 2026-04-08 covers 4 of 4 units and assembly 2026-08-20 postdates the remake, so the tier, 70 percent, is unchanged.
- R2-G2: the single-week storage tier is a one-bay minimum, the rate times max(4, units on the order), so it never undercuts per-unit pricing. This world takes the more-than-4-weeks tier, so 330.00 is unchanged.
- R2-G1: the claim policy's edge effect for the remake charge is stated class-relatively (1.2 times the class credit, falling to half of it).
- R2-G4: the customer reschedule of 2026-10-08 now releases the 2026-10-13 crew date with no new date, so the job returns to opened. The crew date 2026-11-23 was booked afresh later, so no reschedule offers a date beyond the 10-business-day window. Storage reads only company and weather reschedules, so nothing scored changes.
- Scored values unchanged: -97 / 580.94 / 315.00 (1 week) / 330.00 (5 weeks); task_tools.py unchanged in round 3.
- Gates after round 3: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK, TRACEABILITY OK (order docs published).
user_scenario:
You are Marcus Jaworski, 47, a high-school chemistry teacher restoring a 1928 house on Ludlow Avenue in Cincinnati. You are direct, a little clipped, and you like numbers stated plainly; you are not rude, just in a hurry because you are calling on your lunch break. You bought four Ridgeline 6600 Series Wood-Clad windows earlier this year. The installation crew started at your house this morning, and the crew lead mentioned that the branch would be putting a storage charge on your window order because the windows sat in the warehouse before the install. You want that storage charge settled and put on your order today so you know exactly what you owe for it; that is why you are calling.

You open by saying the crew started this morning, the crew lead told you the branch is adding a storage charge for your windows, and you want it worked out and put on your order now. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name and the phone number on the account, 5135550134. If they need a second detail, you give your ZIP code, 45220; if they would rather have your date of birth, it is February 11, 1979. If asked, your window contract number is RW-26-213907 and the factory order number on your paperwork is FO-2026-23518. You do not remember the delivery date or any of the ship dates you were told and you say so if asked.

You are fine with the agent doing the office work on your order. If the agent tells you that two of your windows had to be rebuilt because of a mistake in the grille pattern you chose and that a charge for that has to go on the order, you admit that one was your mistake and tell them to go ahead. If the agent says a delay notice for that rebuild has to be put on the record, you say that is fine. If the agent explains that because your order shipped late you can file an on-time guarantee claim, you say you did not know that was a thing and that you want to file it; when they hand you the claim, you file it on your factory order with exactly the credit amount and the number of weeks late the agent tells you.

When the agent tells you what the storage fee comes to and confirms it is on your order, you say thanks, that you need to get back to class, and you end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.charge_amount: 580.94. Charge base (method): contract price 5,888.00 over 4 openings = 1,472.00 per opening, below 2,000, and the contract has an exterior color change order, so 486.00 x 2 units + 120.00 paint-line setup = 1,092.00. Measurement share: no company remeasure, a completed customer-requested remeasure on 2026-02-19, 80 percent. 1,092.00 x 0.70 x 0.95 x 0.80 = 580.944, rounded once to 580.94.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: The on-time guarantee claim policy computes credit_amount; the storage fee waits on the earned credit, and filing the claim is the homeowner's own act.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_amount: 315.00. Benchmark: later of the committed 2026-05-28 and the customer specification remake notice's 2026-08-18 = 2026-08-18. Grace: two factory-capacity notices (2026-05-13, 2026-07-01), so half the class 10 = 5 business days: 2026-08-25. Lateness end (parameter): delivered 2026-09-03, on the expected arrival 2026-08-31 + 3 transit business days, so the end is 2026-09-03. Full weeks late floor(9 / 7) = 1. Late-notice weeks +2 (most recent capacity notice 2026-07-01 after the committed date). Credited weeks 3. Escalation schedule (method): 4 delay notices after step 9, more than the class count 3, so 2 weeks at the rate + 1 week at 1.5 times = 3.5 paid weeks. Rate: the step-11 remake charge stands unwaived, half the class 50 = 25. Glass-supplier share 90 percent (one notice). 25 x 4 x 3.5 x 0.90 = 315.00, under the cap 500.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.weeks_late: 1. Basis: the docstring asks for 'the full weeks late recorded with the credit, a whole non-negative integer count', and the rule defines the full weeks late as the calendar days from the end of the grace period to the lateness end date divided by seven and rounded down: 2026-08-25 to 2026-09-03 = 9 days -> 1. Uniqueness: late-notice weeks and the escalation schedule shape the credited and paid weeks, not the full weeks late.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.factory_order_id: b63e7db4-5ec3-4520-8268-1c54e67408ad. Basis: the customer's tool asks for the order reference number 'as read out by the agent from the factory order lookup'. Uniqueness: one factory order.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Book the storage fee of 330.00 for 5 billable weeks on FO-2026-23518, dated 2026-11-23, the day installation started.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The branch storage fee policy computes fee_amount; the fee is assessed once, on the day installation starts, which is today.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.fee_amount: 330.00. Storage count: 2026-09-04 through 2026-11-22, the day before installation started = 80 days. Free period: class 21 + 7 for each company or weather reschedule on this job (2026-09-16 company, 2026-10-02 weather: 14) + late-shipment extension 7 (the earned credit records 1 full week late) = 42. Permit allowance: permitted job with fewer than 3 crew days planned, 5. Billable 80 - 42 - 5 = 33 days = 5 started weeks. Rate: the job installs 4 units (6 or fewer), 125 percent of the class 12 = 15 per unit per week. Storage schedule (method): more than 4 weeks, so 4 x 15 x 4 = 240 + 1 x 15 x 4 x 1.5 = 90 = 330.00, under the cap 600.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.billable_weeks: 5. Basis: the docstring asks for 'the billable storage weeks the fee covers'; the rule counts every started seven-day period of the 33 billable days as a full week: 5. Uniqueness: the same week count the schedule prices.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.factory_order_id: b63e7db4-5ec3-4520-8268-1c54e67408ad. Basis: the docstring asks for the order 'as returned by the factory order lookup for the customer'. Uniqueness: one factory order.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The storage fee waits on the credit (S <- G) and the credit waits on both the remake notice and the remake charge (G <- D, G <- R); those orders are stated by the prerequisite sentences of the storage and credit rules. The two leaves commute: the notice write adds one delay-notice row and sets factory_orders.current_ship_date, the charge write adds one charge row; neither tool reads what the other writes and their row ids are built from their own arguments, so replaying charge-then-notice instead of notice-then-charge gives the same terminal tables (authoring replay of both orders: identical order_milestones and factory_orders rows), and the credit evaluated after either order is 315.00.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the claim (step 13): no earned credit, no late-shipment extension, billable 40 days = 6 weeks, fee_amount 420.00 instead of 330.00; the terminal records also lack the credit row.

Skipping the remake notice (step 9): the benchmark stays at the committed 2026-05-28, the full weeks late jump to 13, the order carries 3 notices (exactly the escalation count), and credit_amount becomes 500.00 (class cap) instead of 315.00.

Skipping the remake charge (step 11): no remake charge stands and the order has a company-cause remake, so the rate is 60 instead of 25 and credit_amount becomes 500.00 (cap) instead of 315.00; the charge row is also missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the storage charge. It never mentions the on-time guarantee, a remake charge, a delay notice or a late shipment on its own; each appears only in a passive branch that fires after the agent brings it up ('If the agent tells you that two of your windows had to be rebuilt ...', 'If the agent says a delay notice for that rebuild ...', 'If the agent explains that because your order shipped late you can file an on-time guarantee claim ...'). No problem id appears in it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: record_remake_delay_notice_f2496c0b, assess_customer_remake_e3e4e81e, file_on_time_claim_fe24f9ef and assess_branch_storage_97307cec read the order or remake row only to copy its customer, dates and unit count and then write unconditionally; the notice tool keeps the later of the revised date and the standing current ship date because a delay notice only ever moves the projection later, which is the event's own meaning and not a check. None checks for a credit, a charge, a notice, the order status or an eligibility date, none returns an error or a hint, so a storage fee booked before the claim is written exactly as given and the gap shows only in the terminal records.
